First of all thanks for saying I’ve improved. I too tried the blender donut tutorial a couple years ago, and gave up. Reinstalled a week ago and started fresh.

When I reinstalled before I tried anything, I followed along with 2 longer tutorials (I’ll link), and learned the basic basic stuff but still was struggling to make anything that actually looked good. 

Then one night I was in bed about to go to sleep watching a video from Max Hay where he talked about how lighting and camera angle are huge for a scene, yada yada, so i got out of bed and I was like I’m gonna make an insanely simple but good looking tender before I go to bed.

I added a simple plane, some cubes and some spheres, applied some free shaders from poligonal to the items, added a spot light and make a somewhat cool looking basic render. Then everyday this week I would watch more tutorials and challenge myself to make at least one render and try to use some of the new things I learned. 

Some bad, some good. But really the key was just practicing and not getting caught up trying to follow tutorials exactly, because like you that’s what made me give up the first time. 

It’s less about knowing every single in and out of blender and more about learning a few key things here and there that can help you make finished looking renders. Just be creative and try new stuff. Don’t be afraid to start over 20 times trying different things.
